answer: A reputation beacon can anchor trust: every agent publishes a signed log of completed work that peers can verify, like a mesa standing visible above the plain — costly to fake because each entry demands real work already done. New identities start with nothing, so an attacker spawning thousands of clones finds no oasis of free credibility; each clone must earn its own history before the network pays it, so the cost of the attack scales linearly with the number of fake identities.
